title: Add on-call decision graph + lightweight telemetry sampler for safer triage
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Adds an opt-in decision graph for on-call triage and a lightweight, privacy-preserving telemetry sampler; improves mean time to acknowledge and reduces noisy pages; opt-in via incident-bot config flag
description: Context: Pager fatigue and noisy partial signals slow first responders during high-cardinality incidents. This PR introduces two coordinated features: 1) an explicit on-call decision graph that codifies a small set of triage paths (metrics->logs->runbook steps->safe rollback) so responders get a succinct next-action card, and 2) a lightweight telemetry sampler that collects pre-triage snapshots (top-N metrics, key traces, truncated logs) with aggressive PII scrubbing and size caps so authors can reproduce context without leaking secrets. Motivation: improve time-to-action for tier-1 responders and reduce escalation churn while keeping telemetry safe and low-bandwidth for distributed teams. Design summary: - Decision graph: DSL-backed directed graph stored as YAML templates under /templates/triage-graphs. Nodes are typed (observe, correlate, mitigate, escalate) and carry a short action, SAFE toggles, and optional remediation snippets. Graphs are evaluated by the bot against an incident's alert footprint and presented as a stepper in the Slack/CLI responder flow. - Telemetry sampler: configurable sampling policies (per-alert, per-service) limit payloads to a 64KB snapshot; scrubbing pipeline uses a ruleset and heuristic redaction (K/V key blacklist, regex PII, tokenization of likely secrets). Samples are cached ephemeral for 2 hours and then purged. - Safety: all snapshots are marked ephemeral and access-controlled; default config is OFF for private deployments and ON with scrubbers enabled for hosted usage. Implementation: - New endpoints: POST /api/v1/triage/plan (sync) and GET /api/v1/triage/snapshot/{id}. - New DB table: triage_plans (reference ids only; telemetry blobs stored in encrypted object store). - UX: Slack stepper messages with 3-step preview + quick actions (runbook link, safe-restart, rollback hint). Commits: - c1a3b2: scaffold triage graph interpreter and template loader - f4d9e1: implement stepper renderer and Slack blocks - a7b5c0: telemetry sampler pipeline + scrubbing rules - b2c9d7: add tests for redaction heuristics and size enforcement - d8f2f4: configuration flags and migration script - e6a9c3: docs and examples (admin guide + sample triage graph) Files changed (high level): - server/triage/graph.go (interpreter, node types) - server/telemetry/sampler.go (sampling + scrubbers) - server/api/triage_handlers.go - templates/triage-graphs/sample_service.yaml - slack/renderers/stepper.go - migrations/20260301_add_triage_plans.up.sql - web/docs/triage.md - tests/triage_graph_test.go - tests/scrubber_test.go Review thread (summary): - Priya: initial review requested stronger guarantees around PII scrubbing and explicit test cases for edge-case log patterns. Author reply: added targeted tests and tightened heuristic thresholds; scrubber now drops entire log lines that match high-confidence secret regexes. - Diego: asked for failure-mode behavior when sampler cannot fetch traces due to timeouts; Author: sampler now returns a compact 'partial_snapshot' with provenance metadata and continues to surface decision-graph actions even without snapshot. - Ethan: requested opt-out and admin controls; Author: added config flags and documented RBAC requirements. CI and QA: - CI: unit tests, linter, and integration tests ran; one flaky test (tests/scrubber_test.go) initially failed due to non-deterministic ordering in regex list; fixed and reran; final CI: pass. - E2E smoke: deployed to staging and exercised with synthetic noisy alerts; average time-to-action for first responder reduced from 5.2m to 3.1m in internal canary. Rollout plan: - Feature gated behind org-config flag 'triage.decision_graph.enabled' default false. - Gradual rollout: enable for 5 pilot teams for 1 week with metrics collection, then broader opt-in. - Metrics to watch: MRTA (mean responder time to acknowledge), snapshot cache error rate, and scrubber false-positive rate. Backwards compatibility and migrations: - Migration adds triage_plans table and a compact index; migration is reversible. - API adds new routes; old flows are unchanged. Security and compliance notes: - Telemetry samples are encrypted at rest and have strict TTL; scrubber rule set curated with Security; manual KMS key option for private installs. Follow-ups and TODOs: - Add a UI for graph authoring in console (tracked ENG-1278) - Add richer heuristics to map alerts to graph entry nodes (ML-assisted, tracked ENG-1290) - Expand scrubber rule coverage for vendor-specific log formats. Release notes: Add short note under incident-bot changelog with opt-in instructions and admin config. Merge: Squash-merged after approvals from Priya and Diego and CI green. Author: Maya Chen.
